name: Dansk Vegetarisk Forening: policy work for Denmark's plant-based food fund (charityevals' estimate)
summary: Dansk Vegetarisk Forening (DVF) is Denmark's vegetarian society; this estimate covers its domestic policy work, which over 2020-2024 helped win and then top up and make permanent Denmark's Fund for Plant-Based Foods (675 million kroner for 2023-2030, plus 420 million for 2025-2030 in the 2024 green tripartite agreement), counted as a past average of five years' policy spending against DVF's share of the fund's grants, with 2024 as the year modelled. At the defaults it comes to about 0.28 years of healthy life per $1,000, under a tenth of the median animal charity on the site, because the fund's money changes meals only indirectly (grants for kitchen training, products, export and research: meals_in_project_per_dkk, an estimated 0.025 animal-product meals replaced per krone during the projects, about double with lasting menus) and DVF is one of many groups behind it (attribution_share_shared 0.25). The result is mostly uncertainty: the meals a krone of grants replaces, DVF's share of the credit and the years a won reform counts are judgments that together span four orders of magnitude. DVF's other programme areas (business, education, inspiration, cooperation and international work, about 75% of programme spending) publish no outcome data in meals or animals and are not modelled.

source.title: charityevals' estimate: Dansk Vegetarisk Forening's policy work

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

sections.title: In chicken pain days
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for every animal model. The shared SAD figures are Ambitious Impact's, which count each species' pain as a share of a person's with its own species weights. Here those weights come out and Rethink Priorities' go in, so every species is counted in days of a chicken's disabling pain. How a chicken compares with a person is the one animal slider.

Anchors: DVF's staff page lists nine people under policy work, but six of them work on the EU 'Danish Plant-Based Diplomacy' project (international work, not modelled), leaving three for domestic policy (general secretary, programme chief, a political adviser; DVF's staff page and accounts 2024 note 9, 'Politisk team 249.573') of 18-27 staff in 2022-2024 (about 0.15 by headcount), plus the communication staff who ran the advertising campaigns around both agreements and the general secretary's outsized role; in 2020-2021, with 9-17 staff, DVF describes its work as mostly political (2021 report: donations let it 'focus on the political work'). Weighting each year's share by its real spending (policy spending about 10.2 of 44.5 million kroner over 2020-2024 in 2024 prices) gives about 0.23; 0.25, 0.15-0.4.

rows.label: The fund's yearly budget from both wins, 2025-2030 (DKK)
rows.explainer: 84 million kroner a year from the 2021 appropriation plus 70 million from the top-up: about 154 million a year, close to the grant rounds of 2025 (213 million, of which 50 million a research pool from another agreement) and 2026 (195.5 million kroner to 38 projects, Plantefonden's home page https://www.plantefonden.dk/, retrieved 2026-11-03); the 2025 research pool is on p. 9 of the fund's annual report 2025.

rows.label: Fund grants a year won, per year of the campaign
rows.explainer: The fund's yearly budget in dollars (2024 rate), divided by the five campaign years whose average cost is the cost above: one average year of DVF's policy work is credited with a fifth of the wins. Each won year of grants is counted for the site's years a won reform counts (below).

rows.label: Animal-product meals replaced during the projects, per krone of fund grants
rows.explainer: Our judgment; the fund began measuring effects only in 2025 and no project has reported meals replaced. Anchor: the largest school-food grant of 2025 (10,518,097 kroner) targets at least 1,440,000 plant-based meals over its project period, August 2025 to December 2028, 0.137 plant meals per krone (Plantefonden's annual report 2025, p. 34). Worked: about half the fund's money goes to comparably direct meal projects (57% to demand and 34% to professional kitchens in 2025; the rest to products, export and sector-building, whose effect on Danish meals within the years counted is small); those deliver perhaps 0.1 plant meals per krone once missed targets are allowed for, of which about half replace an animal-product meal that would otherwise have been on the menu: 0.5 × 0.1 × 0.5 = 0.025, from a tenth of that to five times it. Lasting menu changes after the project are the next row; whether projects would have happened anyway and whether diners eat less meat overall are the adjustments, not this row.

rows.label: Meals replaced after the project ends, as a multiple of those during it
rows.explainer: Our judgment: kitchens that changed menus and trained staff keep part of the change after the grant ends; menus drift back and staff turn over. Anchor: in the five-year follow-up of the Danish '6 a day' worksite canteens (Thorsen et al. 2010, Public Health Nutrition 13:1647-52), four of five canteens kept or increased their higher vegetable servings. Worked: about 1.7 project-lengths of after-period × 0.8 of kitchens keeping the change ≈ 1.3, shaded to 1 because plant-based menu changes are newer and less settled than vegetable servings. 1 (as many meals again after the project as during it), from 0 (none) to 2.

rows.label: Length of a fund project (years)

source.title: Fonden for Plantebaserede Fødevarer, Årsberetning 2025
source.quote: Af tabellen ses det også, at hovedparten af projekterne er flerårige.

rows.explainer: Most 2025 projects run two to three and a half years (the school-food project August 2025 to December 2028); the meals after a project come this much later than those during it and are discounted for it.

rows.label: Animal-product meals replaced per krone of fund grants
rows.explainer: Meals during the projects, discounted to the middle of the project, plus those after it, discounted to the middle of the after-period (the persistence multiple in project-lengths, so centred project_years × (1 + multiple/2) after the start). The wait from the win to the first grants is years_until_effect.

rows.label: Animal-product meals replaced per dollar of fund grants
rows.explainer: Per krone converted to per dollar at the 2024 rate.

rows.label: Suffering in a replaced meal in Denmark, relative to the reference meal
rows.explainer: 1, range 0.5-2: no published estimate compares a Danish replaced meal with the site's reference meal (a Latin American canteen meal) the same way, so the site's rule for Denmark applies (docs/normalization.md 2.9; templates.md diet-change). Never a per-meal figure rebuilt from a meat mix of our own.

rows.label: Fall in production per meal not eaten
rows.explainer: Fewer meals bought lowers production by less than one for one, because prices fall and others buy more (Norwood and Lusk 2011); the site's shared figure.

rows.label: SADs averted per dollar of fund grants
rows.explainer: Built from the site's shared diet-change figures, as a direct meal model would be: meals replaced per dollar × the site's one figure for a replaced meal (2024 SADs) × the Danish meal-mix ratio × the production response.

rows.label: Probability the change happens because of this work
rows.explainer: Both wins happened: the fund was legislated in 2023 and the top-up and permanence agreed in November 2024 (observed). Not 1 at the low end only because a later government could cut the fund before the years counted run out. Whether DVF's work caused the wins is the years-brought-forward question below, and its share of the credit is attribution.

rows.label: Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway
rows.explainer: The site's one answer (Your values → How impact is counted; docs/normalization.md 2.9). Never the charity's or an evaluator's own years.

rows.label: Years from the win until the policy takes effect
rows.explainer: From the wins to the grants' effects on meals: the 2021 agreement's first grants came in November 2023, the 2024 top-up's in the 2025 round, and from the 2021 agreement (October 2021) to its first grants (November 2023: 'i november måned 2023, kunne bestyrelsen give tilsagn til de første 36 projekter', https://www.plantefonden.dk/hvem-er-vi/om-plantefonden) is 2.1 years and from the 2024 top-up (November 2024) to its first round's grants (late 2025) about 1.1 years, weighted by the money (84 and 70 million kroner a year) about 1.7; the meals within a project are discounted separately (meals_replaced_per_dkk). 1.7 years, 1.2-3.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the policy takes effect
rows.explainer: The wait discounted at the shared rate, like every future benefit.

rows.label: Discounted years of impact
SADs averted by the wins credited to a year of policy work, before adjustments
Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: How far plant meals served under the fund's projects turn into fewer animal-product meals eaten, in two parts. Compensation: diners can eat more animal products at other meals and at home; in Garnett et al. 2019 (PNAS, Cambridge cafeterias) more vegetarian options cut meat-meal sales without a detectable rise at the evening meal, but that follow-up was small, so about 0.85 (0.6-1). Reporting: the fund grades its own projects' success from their self-reports (annual report 2025, p. 38) and effect measurement began only in 2025, about 0.85 (0.65-0.95). Product about 0.7 (0.4-0.9). The meals judgment above is already net of what was on the menus anyway.

rows.label: Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: The share of the fund's projects that would not have happened without the fund: some grantees would have found other money for part of this work. Anchors: DVF's own grants from the organic farming fund (FØL) fell from 4.98 to 0.50 million kroner between 2023 and 2024 as its plant-fund grants rose to 3.07 million (accounts 2024, note 5), a sign of substitution between public funds; but the fund was about 3.5 times oversubscribed in 2025 (over 750 million kroner sought, 213 million granted; annual report 2025, p. 5), so most funded projects had no other funder ready. Whether the fund itself would have come anyway is counted in the years a won reform counts, not here (Convention 5). 0.7, 0.5-0.9.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: DVF's share of the advocacy resources behind the fund and its top-up. Named partners: Plantebranchen (the plant-based industry association), Økologisk Landsforening and other green organisations in 2021 (DVF's 2021 report); in 2024 Plantebranchen, Rådet for Grøn Omstilling, World Animal Protection, Greenpeace and Klimabevægelsen, plus a joint advertisement with 51 other organisations and companies (DVF's 2024 report, p. 7), and the parties that negotiated it in (SF and Radikale). Worked as staff-years on the fund: DVF about 3 (its domestic policy staff, for whom the fund was a top priority throughout; it holds a seat on the fund's board and co-wrote the 2020 research strategy with Landbrug & Fødevarer and Tænketanken Frej); Plantebranchen and Økologisk Landsforening about 2 each; Landbrug & Fødevarer, Rådet for Grøn Omstilling, Greenpeace, World Animal Protection, Klimabevægelsen and Tænketanken Frej about 1 each: 3 / 13 = 0.23. The parties' own work is not a resource bought, and the years a won reform counts carry whether it would have come anyway. Our judgment 0.25, 0.1-0.5 (each partner's effort could be half or double); the same share serves both credit modes.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Other policy wins of the same campaign, as a share of the modelled value
rows.explainer: Our judgment. The same policy work also won, in the 2021 agreement, 580 million kroner of EU farm support for farmers growing crops for food instead of feed, and the national action plan for plant-based foods (DVF 2021 report, p. 4); and research funding for plant-based food: first place in the 2021 agreement's 350 million kroner green-research pot (same page) and the 50 million kroner research pool run through the fund in 2025 (fund annual report 2025, p. 9), on which DVF set aside 988,000 kroner in 2024 for further work (accounts 2024, note 19). The crop premium works on the supply side (what farmers grow, much of it exported), so its effect on Danish animal-product meals is a small fraction of the fund's per krone; the action plan has no budget of its own; research money works over decades. Together 8%, 0-20%. Not counted: the lawsuits, which secured individual rights rather than menus.

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above, with the other policy wins added as a share.

rows.label: SADs averted per year of policy work
rows.explainer: Only the policy branch applies: DVF moves no money to other charities (its only gifts out were 5,500 kroner of members' gifts passed to a children's home, accounts 2024 note 12) and runs no career-change programme, so the template's money-moved and career branches are left out rather than kept at zero with values in another unit.

rows.label: SADs averted per dollar of policy work
rows.explainer: The past average: a year of DVF's policy work, 2020-2024, against its share of the fund it won. The next dollar is valued below at the shared share of that average.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: DVF's own salaries, pensions and social contributions (note 14) over its 2024 spending: about two-thirds, the shared default for advocacy work (0.65) confirmed by its accounts.
